title: The low-memory search modes spend most of their time in read calls
body:
In the benchmark suite under `benchmarks/`, the `count`, `locate` and `extract` rows with `-l` or `-v` are 5 to 9 times slower than the in-memory row, with about 7 of 8 cores busy. On the 100 MiB index, `count -l` takes 5.6 s against 0.75 s in memory. On a 1 GiB index, before the fixture was cut, `count -l` took 9.5 s of wall and 41 s of system time, and `count -v` 11.6 s of wall and 56 s of system time.

The system time is where the run goes. The disk modes read the suffix array through `Storage::Disk` in `libsufr/src/lib.rs`, one read per probe of the binary search, and the probes of 1,000,000 queries do not share reads.

## Open

- Whether the per-probe reads can be batched, or the probes of one query served from one larger read.
- Whether the rows measure what `-l` and `-v` are for, since every row reads the index from a cold page cache.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/5bf3e231
notes.text: The count, locate and extract rows were removed from benchmarks/ before the suite's second commit, so the numbers above come from the first commit, 1e4005e. Reproducing them means checking that commit out, or adding the rows back with Input::Index and the query file from its synth.rs.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Retyped from bug to feature on 2026-11-03: the results are right in every disk mode, and the per-probe reads are a design to change with a benchmark, not a defect.
